PAN Application & Correction.shortDescription: Assistance with new PAN applications, corrections, modifications, and reprinting with the Income Tax Department.
PAN Application & Correction.longDescription: Whether you need a new PAN or need to correct existing details like name, DOB, or photo, we handle the full application process for fast, error-free processing.
benefits: Avoids rejection due to documentation errors
Support for both individuals and entities

process.title: Document Collection
process.description: Gather identity, address, and correction proofs.

process.title: PAN Delivery
process.description: Receive updated e-PAN and physical card.

faqs.question: Can I correct my date of birth on PAN?
faqs.answer: Yes, with valid supporting proof of the correct date of birth.

faqs.question: How long does correction take?
faqs.answer: Typically 7-10 working days after submission.

faqs.question: Is a new PAN issued after correction?
faqs.answer: No, the same PAN number is retained with updated details.

Income Tax Return Filing.shortDescription: Preparation and filing of income tax returns for individuals, businesses, professionals, and companies.
Income Tax Return Filing.longDescription: We prepare accurate income tax returns after reviewing income sources, deductions, and applicable regime, ensuring timely and compliant filing for every taxpayer category.

process.title: Data Collection
process.description: Gather income, deduction, and TDS details.

process.title: Computation
process.description: Compute taxable income and compare tax regimes.

process.title: Filing
process.description: E-file the return and complete verification.

faqs.question: What is the due date for ITR filing?
faqs.answer: 31st July for individuals without audit requirement, later for audit cases.

faqs.question: What happens if I miss the deadline?
faqs.answer: A belated return can be filed with late fees and interest.

faqs.question: Is e-verification mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, the return must be verified within 30 days of filing.

Revised Income Tax Return.shortDescription: File revised returns to correct omissions, errors, or incorrect information in your original filing.
Revised Income Tax Return.longDescription: If you discover an error after filing, a revised return lets you correct income, deductions, or tax credit details before the assessment is completed.

process.title: Revised Computation
process.description: Recompute income and tax with corrections.

process.title: Filing
process.description: File and verify the revised return.

faqs.question: How many times can I revise a return?
faqs.answer: Multiple times, within the permitted timeline before assessment completion.

faqs.question: What is the deadline for revision?
faqs.answer: Generally 31st December of the assessment year.

faqs.question: Does revision restart the assessment period?
faqs.answer: No, but it does supersede the original return's data.

Belated Income Tax Return.shortDescription: File your income tax return after the due date with applicable interest and late-fee compliance.
Belated Income Tax Return.longDescription: Missing the original deadline doesn't mean losing the ability to file. We prepare and file belated returns while computing applicable interest and late fees correctly.

process.title: Liability Computation
process.description: Compute tax, interest, and late fees.

process.title: Filing
process.description: File and verify the belated return.

faqs.question: What is the last date for belated returns?
faqs.answer: Generally 31st December of the assessment year.

faqs.question: Can losses be carried forward in a belated return?
faqs.answer: Most losses cannot be carried forward, except house property loss.

faqs.question: What is the late fee amount?
faqs.answer: Up to ₹5,000, or ₹1,000 for income below ₹5 lakh.

Updated Income Tax Return.shortDescription: File updated returns to declare additional income or correct earlier returns within statutory timelines.
Updated Income Tax Return.longDescription: Updated returns under Section 139(8A) allow correcting missed income even after the belated/revised return window closes, subject to additional tax payment.
benefits: Second chance to correct past returns
Avoids prosecution risk from unreported income

process.title: Computation
process.description: Compute additional income and applicable extra tax.

process.title: Filing
process.description: File the updated return with payment proof.

faqs.question: What is the time limit for an updated return?
faqs.answer: Within 48 months from the end of the relevant assessment year.

faqs.question: Is additional tax always payable?
faqs.answer: Yes, ranging from 25% to 70% of tax and interest depending on timing.

faqs.question: Can an updated return reduce tax liability?
faqs.answer: No, it can only be filed to report additional income, not reduce liability.

Tax Audit Services.shortDescription: Conduct tax audits under Income Tax provisions and prepare Form 3CD with required disclosures.
Tax Audit Services.longDescription: Businesses and professionals crossing prescribed turnover limits require a tax audit. We conduct the audit, prepare Form 3CD, and ensure timely filing.

faqs.question: Who requires a tax audit?
faqs.answer: Businesses above ₹1 crore turnover (₹10 crore with digital transactions) and professionals above ₹50 lakh receipts.

faqs.question: What is the due date?
faqs.answer: 30th September of the assessment year, generally.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for non-compliance?
faqs.answer: 0.5% of turnover or ₹1.5 lakh, whichever is lower.

Tax Planning & Advisory.shortDescription: Strategic tax planning to legally reduce liability through deductions, exemptions, and structuring.
Tax Planning & Advisory.longDescription: We analyze your income, investments, and business structure to identify legitimate tax-saving opportunities aligned with your financial goals.

faqs.question: Which regime should I choose?
faqs.answer: Depends on your deductions; we compare both to recommend the beneficial one.

faqs.question: Is tax planning different from tax evasion?
faqs.answer: Yes, planning uses legal provisions; evasion is illegal concealment of income.

faqs.question: When should tax planning start?
faqs.answer: Ideally at the start of the financial year for maximum benefit.

TDS Return Filing.shortDescription: Preparation and filing of quarterly TDS statements with deduction, deductee, and challan details.
TDS Return Filing.longDescription: We compile deduction data, verify challan details, and file accurate quarterly TDS returns to avoid defaults and enable timely credit to deductees.

process.title: Return Preparation
process.description: Prepare the applicable TDS return form.

faqs.question: What are the TDS return due dates?
faqs.answer: 31st July, 31st October, 31st January, and 31st May for each quarter.

faqs.question: What happens for incorrect PAN reporting?
faqs.answer: It leads to defaults and denies credit to the deductee.

faqs.question: Is nil TDS return required?
faqs.answer: A declaration of no TDS liability can be filed instead of a nil return.

TDS Registration.shortDescription: Get your TAN application and registration completed to begin tax deduction responsibilities.
TDS Registration.longDescription: Before deducting tax at source, an entity must obtain a TAN and register on the TRACES portal. We manage the entire onboarding process.
benefits: Avoids penalty for non-possession of TAN
Smooth TRACES access for future filings

process.title: Process Setup
process.description: Set up deduction and filing workflow.

faqs.question: Is TAN mandatory before deducting TDS?
faqs.answer: Yes, quoting TAN is compulsory in all TDS-related documents.

faqs.question: Can I use PAN instead of TAN?
faqs.answer: No, except in specific cases like property purchase TDS (Form 26QB).

faqs.question: Is TRACES registration separate from TAN?
faqs.answer: Yes, TRACES access must be registered separately after TAN allotment.

TDS Correction Statement.shortDescription: Correct errors in filed TDS returns including PAN, challan, and deduction discrepancies.
TDS Correction Statement.longDescription: Errors in filed TDS returns can block deductee credit. We identify the discrepancy and file correction statements to resolve it accurately.

process.title: Error Identification
process.description: Review TRACES justification report for defaults.

process.title: Confirmation
process.description: Verify correction is reflected on TRACES.

faqs.question: What causes TDS defaults?
faqs.answer: Incorrect PAN, short deduction, late payment, or challan mismatch.

faqs.question: How many times can a return be corrected?
faqs.answer: Multiple times, as needed to resolve all outstanding defaults.

faqs.question: Does correction affect Form 16/16A?
faqs.answer: Yes, corrected certificates should be reissued after correction.

TDS Reconciliation.shortDescription: Reconcile TDS records with Form 26AS, AIS, and TRACES data to identify differences.
TDS Reconciliation.longDescription: We match your TDS deduction/deposit records against Form 26AS, AIS, and TRACES to ensure accurate credit and identify unreconciled amounts.
benefits: Ensures full and accurate credit claim

process.title: Data Extraction
process.description: Extract Form 26AS, AIS, and books data.

process.title: Reporting
process.description: Provide reconciliation report and next steps.

faqs.question: Why is my TDS credit not reflecting?
faqs.answer: The deductor may not have filed or has misreported the TDS return.

faqs.question: How does this affect my refund?
faqs.answer: Unreconciled TDS can delay or reduce your income tax refund.

faqs.question: What is AIS?
faqs.answer: The Annual Information Statement summarizing your financial transactions and tax data.

TDS Certificate Generation.shortDescription: Prepare and issue applicable TDS certificates including Form 16 and Form 16A within prescribed timelines.
TDS Certificate Generation.longDescription: TDS certificates are essential for deductees to claim credit and file returns. We generate accurate Form 16/16A certificates from TRACES after return filing.
features: Part A and Part B compilation

faqs.question: What is the due date for Form 16?
faqs.answer: 15th June following the financial year.

faqs.question: Is Form 16A quarterly or annual?
faqs.answer: Form 16A is issued quarterly for non-salary TDS.

faqs.question: Can certificates be reissued after correction?
faqs.answer: Yes, updated certificates can be generated post-correction.

TDS Refund & Excess Payment.shortDescription: Assistance in claiming refunds or adjustments for excess TDS deposited or deducted.
TDS Refund & Excess Payment.longDescription: Excess TDS payment due to duplicate challans or over-deduction can be claimed back. We prepare the refund application and coordinate with the department.
benefits: Avoids permanent loss of excess payment

process.title: Excess Identification
process.description: Confirm the excess amount and cause.

faqs.question: Can excess TDS be adjusted against future liability?
faqs.answer: Yes, in many cases adjustment is possible instead of a cash refund.

faqs.question: How long does refund processing take?
faqs.answer: Typically a few weeks depending on department workload.

faqs.question: What causes excess TDS payment?
faqs.answer: Duplicate challans, wrong rate application, or data entry errors.

Income Tax Notice Response.shortDescription: Professional review and response preparation for notices and communications from tax authorities.
Income Tax Notice Response.longDescription: Income tax notices require careful, timely responses. We analyze the notice, gather relevant records, and prepare a clear, well-supported reply.

process.title: Notice Analysis
process.description: Understand the notice type and requirement.

faqs.question: What are common types of notices?
faqs.answer: Notices under Sections 143(1), 139(9), 142(1), and 148, among others.

faqs.question: Is it mandatory to respond?
faqs.answer: Yes, non-response can lead to adverse assessment or penalty.

faqs.question: Can the deadline be extended?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, upon request, at the assessing officer's discretion.

Income Tax Scrutiny Assessment.shortDescription: Representation and assistance during scrutiny assessments including submissions and reconciliations.
Income Tax Scrutiny Assessment.longDescription: Scrutiny assessments involve detailed examination of your return. We prepare comprehensive submissions, reconciliations, and represent you before the assessing officer.

process.title: Case Review
process.description: Understand scope of scrutiny and issues raised.

process.title: Representation
process.description: Attend hearings and respond to queries.

faqs.question: Why was my return selected for scrutiny?
faqs.answer: Risk-based selection, high-value transactions, or mismatches in reporting.

faqs.question: How long does scrutiny take?
faqs.answer: Typically completed within the assessment year timeline set by law.

faqs.question: Can I appeal the scrutiny order?
faqs.answer: Yes, before the Commissioner (Appeals) within the prescribed time.

Income Tax Appeal Services.shortDescription: Preparation and representation for appeals against income tax orders before appellate authorities.
Income Tax Appeal Services.longDescription: When an assessment order is unfavorable, filing a well-drafted appeal is essential. We prepare grounds of appeal and represent your case before the appellate authority.
benefits: Preserves right to challenge adverse orders

process.title: Order Review
process.description: Analyze the order and identify appeal grounds.

process.title: Appeal Drafting
process.description: Prepare Form 35 with statement of facts.

process.title: Filing & Representation
process.description: File appeal and represent at hearings.

faqs.question: What is the time limit for filing an appeal?
faqs.answer: 30 days from receipt of the order.

faqs.question: Is pre-deposit required?
faqs.answer: Generally 20% of disputed demand for a stay on recovery.

faqs.question: Can I appeal further after CIT(A)?
faqs.answer: Yes, to the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT).

Rectification of Income Tax Order.shortDescription: File rectification applications to correct apparent mistakes or errors in income tax orders.
Rectification of Income Tax Order.longDescription: Apparent errors like incorrect tax computation or TDS mismatch can be corrected through a rectification application under Section 154, without a full appeal.
benefits: Quick resolution without full appeal process

process.title: Error Analysis
process.description: Identify the apparent mistake in the order.

process.title: Follow-up
process.description: Track processing until rectified order is passed.

faqs.question: What qualifies as an apparent mistake?
faqs.answer: Errors visible from the record, like computation or TDS mismatch, not debatable issues.

faqs.question: What is the time limit for rectification?
faqs.answer: 4 years from the end of the financial year of the order.

faqs.question: Is rectification different from appeal?
faqs.answer: Yes, rectification is for clear errors; appeal is for disputing the order's merits.

Income Tax Refund Services.shortDescription: Assistance in identifying, claiming, tracking, and resolving income tax refunds.
Income Tax Refund Services.longDescription: We help identify eligible refunds from excess TDS or advance tax, ensure correct claim in the return, and follow up on delayed refund processing.

process.title: Eligibility Review
process.description: Confirm refund amount from filed return.

faqs.question: How long does a refund take?
faqs.answer: Typically 4-6 weeks after processing, sometimes longer.

faqs.question: Why did my refund fail?
faqs.answer: Usually due to unvalidated bank account or mismatched details.

faqs.question: Is interest paid on delayed refunds?
faqs.answer: Yes, interest under Section 244A is generally payable.

Form 26AS & AIS Review.shortDescription: Detailed review of Form 26AS and AIS to reconcile reported income, TDS, and transactions.
Form 26AS & AIS Review.longDescription: We review your Form 26AS and Annual Information Statement to ensure all income, TDS, and high-value transactions are correctly reflected before filing.
features: Feedback submission on AIS, if needed
requirements: Prior year income details for comparison

process.title: Data Retrieval
process.description: Access Form 26AS and AIS from the portal.

process.title: Correction Guidance
process.description: Submit feedback for incorrect entries, if any.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 26AS and AIS?
faqs.answer: 26AS focuses on TDS/TCS; AIS covers a broader range of financial transactions.

faqs.question: Can I dispute incorrect AIS entries?
faqs.answer: Yes, feedback can be submitted directly on the portal.

faqs.question: Should I file based on AIS or my own records?
faqs.answer: Reconcile both and file based on accurate actual income.

Advance Tax Calculation.shortDescription: Calculate advance tax liability and prepare payment schedules to minimize interest exposure.
Advance Tax Calculation.longDescription: We estimate your annual income and compute advance tax instalments due, helping you avoid interest under Sections 234B and 234C.

process.title: Income Estimation
process.description: Project total income for the financial year.

process.title: Payment Guidance
process.description: Provide due dates and payment support.

faqs.question: Who needs to pay advance tax?
faqs.answer: Taxpayers with tax liability above ₹10,000 in a financial year.

faqs.question: What are the due dates?
faqs.answer: 15th June, September, December, and March each year.

faqs.question: What if I underestimate my income?
faqs.answer: Interest applies on the shortfall under Sections 234B/234C.

Self-Assessment Tax Calculation.shortDescription: Compute final tax payable before return filing after considering TDS, advance tax, and interest.
Self-Assessment Tax Calculation.longDescription: Before filing your return, we calculate the balance self-assessment tax due after accounting for TDS, advance tax paid, and applicable interest.
requirements: TDS and advance tax paid details

process.title: Data Compilation
process.description: Gather income, TDS, and advance tax details.

process.title: Computation
process.description: Calculate balance tax and interest payable.

faqs.question: When is self-assessment tax paid?
faqs.answer: Before filing the income tax return, if any balance remains.

faqs.question: What challan is used?
faqs.answer: Challan 280 for self-assessment tax payment.

faqs.question: What if I file without paying due tax?
faqs.answer: The return may be treated as defective until tax is paid.

Capital Gains Tax Computation.shortDescription: Calculate short-term and long-term capital gains on property, shares, and other capital assets.
Capital Gains Tax Computation.longDescription: We accurately compute capital gains considering indexation, holding period, and applicable exemptions across property, securities, and mutual fund transactions.
requirements: Cost of acquisition and improvement details

process.title: Computation
process.description: Calculate gains with indexation as applicable.

faqs.question: What is the difference between STCG and LTCG?
faqs.answer: Based on holding period, taxed at different rates with different benefits like indexation.

faqs.question: Is indexation available for all assets?
faqs.answer: It applies mainly to specific long-term assets like property, subject to current rules.

faqs.question: Can capital losses be set off?
faqs.answer: Yes, against capital gains, with carry-forward provisions for unabsorbed losses.

Capital Gains Tax Planning.shortDescription: Advisory on exemptions, reinvestment options, and strategies to manage capital gains tax liability.
Capital Gains Tax Planning.longDescription: We help plan asset sales and reinvestments to legally minimize capital gains tax through exemptions under Sections 54, 54F, 54EC, and others.
benefits: Reduces capital gains tax liability legally

faqs.question: What is Section 54?
faqs.answer: Exemption on capital gains from residential property upon reinvestment in another house.

faqs.question: What is Section 54EC?
faqs.answer: Exemption via investment in specified capital gains bonds within 6 months.

faqs.question: Is there a cap on exemption amount?
faqs.answer: Yes, certain sections have caps like ₹50 lakh for 54EC bonds.

NRI Income Tax Filing.shortDescription: Specialized income tax filing for NRIs covering Indian income, property, and investments.
NRI Income Tax Filing.longDescription: NRI taxation involves specific rules on residential status, DTAA benefits, and taxable Indian income. We prepare and file returns tailored to NRI circumstances.
benefits: Accurate tax treatment for cross-border income

process.title: Status Determination
process.description: Assess residential status for the year.

process.title: Income Computation
process.description: Compute taxable Indian income and DTAA relief.

process.title: Filing
process.description: E-file the NRI income tax return.

faqs.question: Is global income taxable for NRIs?
faqs.answer: No, only income earned or accrued in India is taxable for NRIs.

faqs.question: Can NRIs claim DTAA benefits?
faqs.answer: Yes, subject to furnishing a Tax Residency Certificate.

faqs.question: Is filing mandatory if TDS is already deducted?
faqs.answer: Yes, filing may still be required, and can help claim refunds.

Foreign Income & Asset Disclosure.shortDescription: Assistance in reporting foreign income, investments, and bank accounts as required under Indian tax law.
Foreign Income & Asset Disclosure.longDescription: Resident taxpayers must disclose foreign assets and income in Schedule FA of their return. We ensure complete and accurate disclosure to avoid heavy penalties.
benefits: Avoids severe Black Money Act penalties
Peace of mind for globally mobile taxpayers
requirements: Foreign tax paid certificates, if any

process.title: Asset Identification
process.description: List all foreign assets and accounts held.

process.title: Disclosure Preparation
process.description: Prepare Schedule FA and related disclosures.

process.title: Filing
process.description: Include disclosures in the income tax return.

faqs.question: Who must disclose foreign assets?
faqs.answer: Resident and ordinarily resident taxpayers holding foreign assets.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for non-disclosure?
faqs.answer: Up to ₹10 lakh under the Black Money Act, per year of default.

faqs.question: Does a small foreign account need disclosure?
faqs.answer: Yes, disclosure applies regardless of the account balance, with limited exceptions.

Presumptive Taxation Return.shortDescription: File returns under presumptive taxation schemes for eligible businesses and professionals.
Presumptive Taxation Return.longDescription: Presumptive taxation under Sections 44AD/44ADA simplifies compliance by taxing a fixed percentage of turnover, removing the need for detailed books.

process.title: Income Computation
process.description: Compute presumptive income at prescribed rate.

faqs.question: What is the presumptive income rate?
faqs.answer: 8% (6% for digital receipts) for business, 50% for eligible professionals.

faqs.question: Is audit required under presumptive scheme?
faqs.answer: Generally no, unless income is declared below the prescribed rate.

faqs.question: Can I switch out of the scheme freely?
faqs.answer: Switching out has restrictions on re-entry for five years in some cases.

Business Income Tax Return.shortDescription: Preparation and filing of returns for proprietorships, firms, and businesses based on accounting records.
Business Income Tax Return.longDescription: We compute business income after considering all allowable expenses, depreciation, and tax provisions, ensuring accurate filing for your business structure.
features: Profit and loss computation from books

faqs.question: Which ITR form applies to businesses?
faqs.answer: ITR-3 for proprietorships/professionals with books, ITR-5 for firms.

faqs.question: Is audit mandatory for all businesses?
faqs.answer: Only above prescribed turnover thresholds, unless under presumptive scheme.

faqs.question: Can losses be carried forward?
faqs.answer: Yes, subject to timely filing and applicable carry-forward rules.

Professional Income Tax Return.shortDescription: Preparation of returns for consultants, doctors, lawyers, architects, and other professionals.
Professional Income Tax Return.longDescription: Professional income has unique deduction and presumptive-scheme considerations. We tailor the return to your specific practice and expense structure.
benefits: Optimized deduction claims for practice expenses
Correct scheme selection for lower tax
requirements: Asset details for depreciation, if applicable

process.title: Computation
process.description: Compute taxable income under applicable scheme.

process.title: Filing
process.description: File ITR-3 or ITR-4 as applicable.

faqs.question: Can professionals opt for presumptive taxation?
faqs.answer: Yes, under Section 44ADA if receipts are within the prescribed limit.

faqs.question: What expenses can professionals claim?
faqs.answer: Office rent, staff salary, professional fees, and other business-related costs.

faqs.question: Is maintaining books mandatory?
faqs.answer: Required if not opting for presumptive taxation or above specified income/receipts.

Company Income Tax Return.shortDescription: Preparation and filing of corporate income tax returns considering deductions and applicable provisions.
Company Income Tax Return.longDescription: We prepare corporate tax returns after reviewing financial statements, tax adjustments, MAT computation, and depreciation to ensure accurate, compliant filing.
features: Financial statement review and tax adjustments
Depreciation as per Income Tax rules

process.title: Financial Review
process.description: Review financials and tax audit report.

faqs.question: What is the due date for company returns?
faqs.answer: 31st October following the financial year, if audit is applicable.

faqs.question: What is MAT?
faqs.answer: Minimum Alternate Tax, applicable when tax under normal provisions is lower.

faqs.question: Is tax audit mandatory for all companies?
faqs.answer: Yes, for companies above specified turnover; typically applicable for most companies.

LLP Income Tax Return.shortDescription: Preparation and filing of LLP income tax returns including deductions and partner disclosures.
LLP Income Tax Return.longDescription: We compute LLP taxable income after accounting for partner remuneration, interest, and applicable deductions, ensuring accurate ITR-5 filing.

process.title: Financial Review
process.description: Review LLP books and agreement terms.

faqs.question: Is LLP taxed like a company?
faqs.answer: LLPs are taxed at a flat rate, distinct from company tax slabs, with no dividend distribution tax.

faqs.question: Can partner remuneration be deducted?
faqs.answer: Yes, subject to limits prescribed under Section 40(b).

faqs.question: Is audit mandatory for all LLPs?
faqs.answer: Only if turnover/contribution exceeds prescribed thresholds.

Partnership Firm Tax Filing.shortDescription: Tax computation and return filing for partnership firms including remuneration and deductions.
Partnership Firm Tax Filing.longDescription: We compute firm income considering partner remuneration, interest on capital, and depreciation, ensuring compliant ITR-5 filing for the firm.

process.title: Deed Review
process.description: Verify remuneration/interest clauses in the deed.

process.title: Computation
process.description: Compute taxable income per applicable limits.

faqs.question: Are partnership firms taxed at flat rates?
faqs.answer: Yes, generally at 30% plus applicable surcharge and cess.

faqs.question: Can remuneration exceed deed limits?
faqs.answer: No, only remuneration within Section 40(b) limits is deductible.

faqs.question: Do partners pay tax again on their share?
faqs.answer: No, a partner's share of firm profit is exempt in their individual hands.

Trust & NGO Income Tax Filing.shortDescription: Preparation and filing of returns for trusts, societies, and charitable institutions with applicable exemptions.
Trust & NGO Income Tax Filing.longDescription: We prepare returns for trusts and NGOs considering exemption conditions, application of income, and audit requirements under the applicable provisions.

faqs.question: What is the minimum application of income required?
faqs.answer: 85% of income must generally be applied for charitable purposes.

faqs.question: Is audit mandatory for trusts?
faqs.answer: Yes, if income before exemption exceeds the basic exemption limit.

faqs.question: What happens if exemption conditions are violated?
faqs.answer: Exemption may be denied and income taxed at applicable rates.

Charitable Trust Tax Compliance.shortDescription: Assistance with exemption requirements, application of income, and audit reports for charitable trusts.
Charitable Trust Tax Compliance.longDescription: We provide ongoing compliance support for charitable trusts covering registration renewal, income application rules, and Form 10B/10BB audit reporting.
features: Application and accumulation of income review

process.title: Filing
process.description: Complete filings and renewals as due.

faqs.question: How often is 12A registration renewed?
faqs.answer: Every 5 years under the current provisional/regular registration regime.

faqs.question: What is accumulation of income?
faqs.answer: Unspent income set aside for future charitable use under Section 11(2).

faqs.question: Is 80G registration separate from 12A?
faqs.answer: Yes, 80G enables donor tax deduction, while 12A exempts the trust's own income.

Tax Deduction Advisory.shortDescription: Advisory on eligible deductions for investments, insurance, housing loans, and other expenditures.
Tax Deduction Advisory.longDescription: We review your financial profile to identify all eligible deductions under Chapter VI-A and other provisions, helping you optimize tax savings.

faqs.question: What is the limit under Section 80C?
faqs.answer: ₹1.5 lakh per year across eligible investments and expenses.

faqs.question: Are deductions available under the new regime?
faqs.answer: Very limited; most Chapter VI-A deductions apply only under the old regime.

faqs.question: Can I claim both HRA and home loan deduction?
faqs.answer: Yes, under specific circumstances such as owning a house in a different city.

Tax Exemption Advisory.shortDescription: Guidance on available exemptions relating to salary, house property, capital gains, and other income.
Tax Exemption Advisory.longDescription: We identify applicable exemptions across income categories to ensure you're not paying more tax than necessary, backed by correct documentation.

faqs.question: Is HRA exemption available under the new regime?
faqs.answer: No, most salary exemptions are not available under the new tax regime.

faqs.question: What is LTA exemption?
faqs.answer: Exemption on travel costs within India, subject to conditions and frequency limits.

faqs.question: Can exemptions be claimed without proof?
faqs.answer: No, proper documentary evidence must be retained and may be requested.

Salary Tax Computation.shortDescription: Calculate taxable salary after considering allowances, perquisites, deductions, and regime provisions.
Salary Tax Computation.longDescription: We compute your accurate taxable salary income, factoring in allowances, perquisites, and applicable exemptions under both tax regimes.
benefits: Identifies regime with lower tax outgo
requirements: Other income details for regime comparison

process.title: Computation
process.description: Calculate taxable salary under both regimes.

faqs.question: What are common salary perquisites?
faqs.answer: Rent-free accommodation, company car, ESOPs, and other employer-provided benefits.

faqs.question: Which regime is better for salaried individuals?
faqs.answer: Depends on total deductions claimed; comparison is recommended each year.

faqs.question: Is standard deduction available?
faqs.answer: Yes, a standard deduction applies under both tax regimes for salaried taxpayers.

HRA Tax Exemption Calculation.shortDescription: Calculate eligible House Rent Allowance exemption based on salary, rent, and location.
HRA Tax Exemption Calculation.longDescription: We compute the least of the three prescribed HRA exemption limits based on your basic salary, rent paid, and city of residence, ensuring maximum eligible relief.
features: Basic salary and rent data collection
Documentation checklist (rent receipts, PAN of landlord)
requirements: Landlord PAN, if rent exceeds ₹1 lakh/year

process.title: Data Collection
process.description: Gather salary and rent payment details.

process.title: Computation
process.description: Calculate exemption using the prescribed formula.

faqs.question: Is HRA exemption available if I don't pay rent?
faqs.answer: No, exemption requires actual rent payment with documentation.

faqs.question: Is landlord PAN mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, if annual rent exceeds ₹1 lakh.

faqs.question: Can I claim HRA and own a house elsewhere?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you genuinely reside on rent in a different city for work.

Income from House Property.shortDescription: Compute taxable rental income, deemed rental income, and eligible deductions under house property provisions.
Income from House Property.longDescription: We calculate income from let-out or self-occupied property considering municipal taxes, standard deduction, and home loan interest deductions.

process.title: Property Data Collection
process.description: Gather rent, tax, and loan details.

process.title: Computation
process.description: Calculate taxable income from the property.

faqs.question: Is self-occupied property taxable?
faqs.answer: Generally no annual value, but interest deduction is still available up to a limit.

faqs.question: What is the interest deduction limit?
faqs.answer: ₹2 lakh per year for self-occupied property under the old regime.

faqs.question: Can house property loss be carried forward?
faqs.answer: Yes, for up to 8 assessment years if not fully set off.

Rental Income Tax Filing.shortDescription: Report rental income accurately with applicable deductions, interest, and expenses.
Rental Income Tax Filing.longDescription: We compute your net taxable rental income after standard deduction and eligible interest, ensuring correct filing under house property provisions.
requirements: Home loan interest certificate, if applicable

process.title: Data Collection
process.description: Gather rental and property loan details.

process.title: Filing
process.description: Include in the income tax return.

faqs.question: Is rental income taxed under a separate head?
faqs.answer: Yes, under 'Income from House Property'.

faqs.question: Can I deduct maintenance charges from rent?
faqs.answer: No, only municipal taxes and the standard 30% deduction are allowed.

faqs.question: What if I own multiple rented properties?
faqs.answer: Each property's income is computed separately and consolidated in the return.

Tax Residency Certificate Advisory.shortDescription: Assistance with tax residency documentation and treaty-related requirements for cross-border taxpayers.
Tax Residency Certificate Advisory.longDescription: A Tax Residency Certificate supports treaty benefit claims for taxpayers earning income in multiple jurisdictions. We assist with application and documentation.

process.title: Status Assessment
process.description: Determine residency status and treaty applicability.

process.title: Application Filing
process.description: File for the residency certificate as applicable.

process.title: Documentation
process.description: Compile records for treaty benefit claims.

faqs.question: Who needs a Tax Residency Certificate?
faqs.answer: Taxpayers claiming DTAA benefits on cross-border income.

faqs.question: Is Form 10F required with TRC?
faqs.answer: Yes, in addition to the TRC issued by the foreign tax authority.

faqs.question: How long is a TRC valid?
faqs.answer: Typically for the specific financial year it is issued for.

DTAA Tax Advisory.shortDescription: Advisory on Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements for exemptions, credits, and treaty benefits.
DTAA Tax Advisory.longDescription: We analyze applicable DTAA provisions between India and the relevant country to determine tax treatment, withholding rates, and available relief.
benefits: Avoids double taxation on cross-border income
requirements: Nature and source of foreign income
Tax paid in the foreign country

process.title: Income Review
process.description: Understand the cross-border income and source country.

process.title: Treaty Analysis
process.description: Identify applicable DTAA provisions and rates.

faqs.question: What is DTAA?
faqs.answer: An agreement between countries to avoid taxing the same income twice.

faqs.question: What are the relief methods under DTAA?
faqs.answer: Exemption method or tax credit method, depending on the treaty.

faqs.question: Is TRC mandatory to claim DTAA benefit?
faqs.answer: Yes, along with Form 10F and other prescribed documents.

Foreign Tax Credit Claim.shortDescription: Assistance in claiming credit for taxes paid outside India against eligible Indian tax liability.
Foreign Tax Credit Claim.longDescription: We compute eligible foreign tax credit based on DTAA provisions and ensure correct claim through Form 67 filing to avoid double taxation.
benefits: Avoids double taxation on foreign income

process.title: Documentation Review
process.description: Gather foreign tax and income proofs.

process.title: Filing
process.description: File Form 67 and claim credit in return.

faqs.question: When must Form 67 be filed?
faqs.answer: Before filing the income tax return for the relevant year.

faqs.question: Is credit available for all foreign taxes?
faqs.answer: Only for taxes covered under the applicable DTAA or specified rules.

faqs.question: What if Form 67 is filed late?
faqs.answer: Credit may still be allowed in genuine cases based on relevant case law and circulars.

Form 67 Filing.shortDescription: Prepare and file Form 67 to claim foreign tax credit against eligible foreign income.
Form 67 Filing.longDescription: Form 67 is mandatory to claim foreign tax credit. We compile foreign income and tax details and file the form accurately before your return deadline.
features: Foreign income and tax data compilation
benefits: Enables valid foreign tax credit claim

process.title: Data Compilation
process.description: Gather foreign income and tax paid details.

process.title: Filing
process.description: Submit Form 67 online before ITR filing.

faqs.question: Is Form 67 filed separately from ITR?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is filed on the e-filing portal before the ITR.

faqs.question: What happens if I forget to file it?
faqs.answer: Foreign tax credit may be denied, though relief has been granted in some cases via condonation.

faqs.question: Is a CA certificate required with Form 67?
faqs.answer: Not always mandatory, but documentation should support the credit claimed.

Tax Deducted at Source Advisory.shortDescription: Advisory on TDS applicability, rates, thresholds, and compliance requirements for various transactions.
Tax Deducted at Source Advisory.longDescription: We help you understand which payments attract TDS, at what rate and threshold, ensuring your business deducts correctly and avoids default.

process.title: Rate Determination
process.description: Apply correct section, rate, and threshold.

faqs.question: What happens if TDS is not deducted?
faqs.answer: The expense may be disallowed and interest/penalty may apply.

faqs.question: Is TDS applicable on all payments?
faqs.answer: No, only on specified categories above prescribed thresholds.

faqs.question: Can excess TDS deducted be refunded?
faqs.answer: Yes, through the deductee's income tax return.

Tax Collected at Source Advisory.shortDescription: Guidance on TCS applicability, rates, procedures, and compliance for specified transactions.
Tax Collected at Source Advisory.longDescription: We help identify TCS obligations on specified sales, remittances, or receipts, and guide you through collection, deposit, and return filing.

process.title: Rate Determination
process.description: Apply correct TCS rate and threshold.

faqs.question: What transactions attract TCS?
faqs.answer: Sale of specified goods, foreign remittances under LRS, and certain other transactions.

faqs.question: Can TCS be claimed as credit?
faqs.answer: Yes, in the collectee's income tax return.

faqs.question: Is TCS the same as TDS?
faqs.answer: No, TCS is collected by the seller, while TDS is deducted by the payer.

TDS/TCS Compliance Review.shortDescription: Comprehensive review of TDS and TCS deductions, deposits, returns, and potential deficiencies.
TDS/TCS Compliance Review.longDescription: We conduct a full review of your TDS/TCS processes to identify short deduction, late deposit, or reporting errors before they attract penalties.

process.title: Scope Definition
process.description: Define review period and transaction types.

faqs.question: How often should this review be done?
faqs.answer: Annually, or quarterly for businesses with high transaction volumes.

faqs.question: What triggers TDS/TCS scrutiny?
faqs.answer: Return mismatches, short deduction, or default notices from TRACES.

faqs.question: Can past defaults be corrected?
faqs.answer: Yes, through correction statements and payment of applicable interest.

Tax Due Diligence.shortDescription: Review tax records, returns, and litigation history to identify potential risks before major transactions.
Tax Due Diligence.longDescription: Before mergers, acquisitions, or investments, a tax due diligence uncovers hidden liabilities, pending disputes, and compliance gaps requiring attention.
benefits: Uncovers hidden tax liabilities before deals

process.title: Scope Definition
process.description: Define review period and key risk areas.

process.title: Detailed Review
process.description: Examine returns, orders, and compliance records.

process.title: Report Delivery
process.description: Present risk findings with quantified exposure.

faqs.question: When is tax due diligence needed?
faqs.answer: Before M&A, investment rounds, or major restructuring.

faqs.question: Does it cover both direct and indirect tax?
faqs.answer: It can be scoped to cover income tax, GST, and other applicable taxes.

faqs.question: What deliverable is provided?
faqs.answer: A detailed report of identified risks with recommended mitigations.

Income Tax Compliance Review.shortDescription: Periodic review of income tax obligations, returns, and documentation to identify potential issues.
Income Tax Compliance Review.longDescription: This proactive review assesses your overall income tax compliance health, flagging gaps in filing, payments, and documentation before they escalate.
benefits: Peace of mind for taxpayers and businesses

process.title: Scope Definition
process.description: Define the review period and focus areas.

faqs.question: How often should this review be done?
faqs.answer: Annually is recommended for individuals and businesses alike.

faqs.question: Does this replace a tax audit?
faqs.answer: No, it's a broader internal health check, not a statutory requirement.

faqs.question: What issues does it commonly surface?
faqs.answer: Missed deductions, late payments, and unreconciled TDS credits.

Tax Litigation & Representation.shortDescription: Professional representation before income tax authorities and appellate forums for disputes and appeals.
Tax Litigation & Representation.longDescription: We represent taxpayers through the full litigation cycle — assessments, appeals, and tribunal proceedings — building a strong, well-documented case at each stage.
requirements: Books of accounts and supporting evidence

process.title: Case Assessment
process.description: Review the dispute and build strategy.

faqs.question: How long does tax litigation take?
faqs.answer: It varies widely, from months to years depending on the forum and complexity.

faqs.question: Can representation reduce tax demand?
faqs.answer: Yes, strong representation often results in relief or reduced demand.

faqs.question: What forums are involved?
faqs.answer: Assessing Officer, CIT(A), ITAT, and higher courts as applicable.

Tax Demand Verification.shortDescription: Review outstanding tax demands, assessment records, and available remedies for incorrect demands.
Tax Demand Verification.longDescription: Outstanding demand notices are sometimes based on errors. We verify the demand against your records and pursue correction or resolution as applicable.
features: Rectification or response filing, as needed

process.title: Demand Review
process.description: Verify demand against assessment and payment records.

process.title: Remedy Identification
process.description: Determine rectification, response, or payment path.

faqs.question: Why do incorrect demands arise?
faqs.answer: Unmatched TDS credit, processing errors, or duplicate demand entries.

faqs.question: Can I dispute a demand online?
faqs.answer: Yes, through the response to outstanding demand feature on the portal.

faqs.question: What happens if I ignore a demand?
faqs.answer: Recovery proceedings and interest may follow, so timely action is important.
